page: Microsoft Azure M208ms_v2 is a memory-optimized server belonging to the MSv2 family. It features 208 dedicated vCPUs powered by Intel Xeon 8280L processors running at 2.7 GHz, built on the x86_64 architecture with 104 physical cores and hyper-threading enabled. The hardware configuration includes a massive 5700.0 GB of system memory, yielding 27.4 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled with a capacity of 4194 GB, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. Virtualization is managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data reveals a significant contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores, fall into the bottom 25%. Conversely, multi-core and parallelized execution metrics are highly competitive. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression both rank in the top 10% tier. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate strong capabilities, with cached read-only small block bandwidth reaching 10453.04 GB/sec in the top 10% and uncached large block read/write bandwidths scoring in the top 25%. Redis SET operations also achieve top-tier performance at 149.33 million operations per second.

The primary tradeoff of the M208ms_v2 is its lower single-threaded efficiency, as evidenced by weak single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. However, its massive memory footprint and high resource density make it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that require massive in-memory datasets rather than raw single-core speed. This server is highly suited for large-scale database operations, in-memory caching systems like Redis, enterprise ERP systems, and heavy multi-threaded data processing pipelines.
